narration: This is Cosmos Semantic: an open-source semantic layer that makes AI agents get the number right, and prove it.
Getting started is one command: pip install cosmos-semantic.

title: bash: ~
narration: Install it with the drivers for the databases you already use.

cmd: cosmos init shop && cd shop && cosmos demo-data
title: bash: ~/shop
narration: Create a project with the example model, and load synthetic e-commerce data into a local DuckDB file.

cmd: cosmos query revenue average_order_value --by orders.status --order orders.status --evidence
narration: Ask for a governed metric. The answer carries its evidence: the formula, the reference date, the source, and fingerprints to reproduce it.
Now, five real databases running in Docker: PostgreSQL, SQL Server, MySQL, MariaDB and Oracle.
Each one is just a line in connections.yml. The semantic model does not change.

cmd: for db in postgres sqlserver mysql mariadb oracle; do cosmos demo-data --target $db; done
narration: Load the same data into all of them.

cmd: for db in local postgres sqlserver mysql mariadb oracle; do echo "-- $db"; COSMOS_DATA_SOURCE=$db cosmos query revenue --by orders.status --order orders.status; done
narration: Same question, six engines, the same number. Cosmos writes the SQL for each dialect, and the test suite checks it on every change.
And when an AI agent asks for customer emails, the request is refused. Personal data never reaches an agent.
For the people who decide, there is a console. Can we trust the numbers? Every governed metric, with its health and its owner.
Every answer an agent received is audited: the rules applied, the row filters, and the exact SQL.
Business processes become a graph, from source systems to metrics.
Cosmos Semantic. Open source, Apache 2.0. Try the live demo, no install needed.
